Before starting, let us learn how light ray refracts in a convex lens. If we know three special rules of the refraction of light through convex lens, we can describe how the image is formed .

(i) If the rays of light is centripetal (Figure 9.23, YO or XO ray) it goes straight after refraction.

(ii) The rays which are parallel with the principle axis, (Figure 9.23, XO) will (CT) pass through focal point (F) after refraction.

(iii) If the direction of the light ray is reversed then it goes back the way it came. Therefore, if any ray goes (Figure 9.23, TC) through the focus then it will be refracted in parallel (CX)

Now we can form the image for a convex lens.
